Rejected pure 'template' because the >40%-owned core alone cannot gain rank, and rejected 'aggressive differential' because GW3's defining feature is a ~125% EO template captain (Haaland, MCI v COV at home) - fading him is uncompensated downside. The proven elite pattern is: own and captain the field's premium so the biggest single swing is neutral, then take rank from the cheap-defender/low-owned end of the squad where variance is cheap.

captain_reasoning.vs_protocol: CLAUDE.md's LOCKED rule (captain = season cum_pts leader, nailed non-GK premium) was calibrated on a squad that does not own Haaland; within that squad it correctly returns B.Fernandes. As an independent manager I own Haaland, and the rule's intent - captain the nailed premium with the highest accumulated scoring rate - is satisfied by the game's most-owned striker at home to the fdr5 away side. B.Fernandes is the vice, so the protocol pick still covers a Haaland non-start.
captain_reasoning.eo_argument: Haaland carries ~125% effective ownership (69.9% owned x ~55% captaincy). Captaining anything else while owning him is a one-sided bet: I gain only if he blanks AND my alternative hauls, and I lose ~25 net points if he returns 12+. Top10k managers do not take that trade in a single gameweek with no chip on the table.
captain_reasoning.differential_captain_considered_and_reje: Lewis-Potter/Gakpo (sub-8%) have real ceilings but a punt captain compounds the field's largest correlated swing. Variance is taken in the 4th-11th XI slots instead, where it is cheap.
captain_reasoning.gemini_kayode_captaincy: Independently reached the same verdict as intel: captaining a 4.6m defender caps the ceiling at ~13 and is a defence-weighted-xpts artefact. Rejected.

chip_reasoning: No chip. fixture-room confirms dgw:false for all 20 teams and no blanks in the GW1-GW5 window, so TC (requires confirmed DGW), BB (requires 10+ doubling) and FH (requires 4+ blanking starters) all fail their CLAUDE.md gates. Squad is freshly built with zero rotation-risk flags, so no WC case either.
transfers_note: Fresh independent build for GW3 - no incumbent squad, therefore zero transfers and zero hits. Forward plan: Yalcouye and Rushworth are the designated funding levers; Cherki (MCI 7.7, net_rate 48.1) and Semenyo (MCI 8.5) are the GW5+ upgrade targets once the NEW triple-up unwinds.

projection_method.priors: Same WRPPM-5D priors sim-lab uses: 0.70*season_ppg + 0.30*recent_form for scoring rate, xgi_per90 shrunk to positional priors on the 2-game sample, then scaled by GW3 FDR and home/away.
projection_method.ev_source: sim-lab MC EV used directly where published (B.Fernandes 8.76, Joao Pedro 6.84, Calafiori 4.95). Remaining players estimated with the same mapping calibrated on sim-lab's own xpts->MC EV ratios (defenders ~1.3-1.7x cache xpts; forwards uplifted to correct the documented clean-sheet/defence bias in xpts.json that deflates strikers).

known_risks: Newcastle triple-up (Hall, Elanga, Wissa) is a correlated block - one flat NEW performance costs three starters at once. Accepted because NEW is fdr3 at home and all three are in positive form/price momentum.
Zero Arsenal and zero Chelsea coverage beyond Calafiori and Joao Pedro, so the ARS v CHE match is a low-exposure fixture for me by design - the opposite of the collision risk intel flagged.
Haaland captaincy is field-neutral, not field-beating: if he hauls I merely keep pace with ~55% of managers. Rank has to come from Lewis-Potter/Ajayi/Gakpo.

Prices sourced from live cache figures surfaced in data-lab/intel/market-desk; features.json is a 2026-07-23 preseason snapshot (target_gw 1, selected_by_pct all 0.0, net_transfers all 0) and was used only for FDR structure, not for live pricing or ownership.
